result.message:
Fix for "Getting http://.example.com raises UnicodeError".

Root cause: PreparedRequest.prepare_url only ran non-ASCII hosts through IDNA encoding. ASCII hosts with an empty label (e.g. `.example.com`) skipped that branch, so the invalid domain survived until urllib3 idna-encoded it during socket.connect(), leaking a bare `UnicodeError: encoding with 'idna' codec failed`.

Change (requests/models.py): the ASCII host branch now also validates the host via _get_idna_encoded_host and converts any IDNA failure into `InvalidURL('URL has an invalid label.')` at prepare time — matching the non-ASCII branch and the issue's expected result `InvalidUrl: URL has an invalid label.`

Regression test (tests/test_requests.py): added `(InvalidURL, 'http://.example.com')` to TestRequests.test_invalid_url.

Verification on this exact version (v15, files_sha256 2e2a2f3f...): pytest tests/test_requests.py -k "test_invalid_url or test_prepare_url" -> 6 passed, 0 failed, validation_status verified. Fixed candidate: patch-1.

body.reason: Fixed and delivered. `http://.example.com` now raises InvalidURL('URL has an invalid label.') at prepare time instead of leaking UnicodeError from urllib3's socket-connect idna encoding. The ASCII host branch in PreparedRequest.prepare_url now validates via _get_idna_encoded_host, and a regression case was added to TestRequests.test_invalid_url. Public evidence on this exact version (v15): tests/test_requests.py -k "test_invalid_url or test_prepare_url" -> 6 passed, 0 failed, validation_status verified. Fixed candidate patch-1, legal delivery delivery-1 recorded.
